cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Carry This with Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Take half Mum's care-home forms. Being her children can't mean I'm the paperwork child.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then sit beside me. I'll explain, and you can write.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. It asks for one main contact.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put yourself. I'll help with every answer, but Mum needs to know she can reach either of us.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders half the forms as shared filial duty; A3 assigns writing under A guidance and A5 appoints B main contact while retaining help, merging supervision with burden sharing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 expertise objection causes A3 teach/write split; B4 one-contact field causes A5 B appointment. Main contact does not mean only reachable child.

relationship.evidence: B2 lacks confidence and B4 starts the form, so A uses cooperation rather than inventing resistance.

heightening.evidence: B4 single contact could restore unequal responsibility; A5 gives B that role while promising shared answers.
